title: Re-FORC: Adaptive Reward Prediction for Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
claim: Prediction quality of the learned forecaster improves steadily as reasoning progresses, consistently across model sizes.
layout: 3 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, shared legend below, shaded error bands
description: A single row of three line plots that share the x-axis, Reasoning Progress (%), running from 0 to 100 in steps of 10. The left panel shows Pearson's rho, which rises from about 0.4–0.5 to about 0.65–0.73. The middle panel shows MSE, which falls from about 0.14 to about 0.08–0.095. The right panel shows MAE, which falls from about 0.33 to about 0.21–0.24. Each panel has three lines with circular markers and translucent shaded variance bands. The lines are Qwen3 1.7B in dark blue, 4B in brown and 8B in cyan. A boxed legend sits centered beneath the panels. The eye goes first to the clear upward or downward trends. The 4B model is slightly best at late progress. The plots are clean, with light dashed gridlines and serif fonts.
caption: Forecast performance with reasoning progress. Cumulative prediction performance of Re-FORC for Qwen3 [ref] models, averaged across four math benchmarks (MATH500, AMC 2024, AIME 2024, and AIME 2025): at each reasoning-progress level, the forecaster is conditioned on the chain-of-thought prefix and predicts the reward ([ref]) at all remaining horizons; we report the agreement between these predictions and the empirically realized success rates ([ref]) at those horizons---i.e., the quality of the full forecast curve, not just a next-step estimate. (left) Pearson correlation $\rho$ (higher is better); (middle) mean squared error (MSE, lower is better); (right) mean absolute error (MAE, lower is better). Forecast quality improves with reasoning progress. Per-dataset results are in Appendix [ref].
abstract: We propose Re-FORC, an adaptive reward prediction method that, given a query, enables prediction of the expected future rewards as a function of the number of future thinking tokens. Re-FORC trains a lightweight adapter on reasoning models, demonstrating improved prediction with longer reasoning and larger models. Re-FORC enables: 1) early stopping of unpromising reasoning chains, reducing compute by up to 26\% compared to fixed-budget cutoffs, while maintaining accuracy, 2) optimized model and thinking length selection that outperforms the largest model alone--- reaching 1.7 percentage points higher peak accuracy while needing up to 12\% less compute to match the largest model's accuracy, 3) adaptive test-time scaling, which increases accuracy by 9.9 percentage points (on average at maximum compute) over confidence-based baselines. Re-FORC allows dynamic reasoning with length control via cost-per-token thresholds while estimating computation time upfront.
